events.note: He was an official at the Han court in China.

events.title: The Hudson's Bay Company is chartered
events.note: Granted a vast fur-trading territory in North America.

events.title: Nokia is founded as a paper mill
events.note: Founded by mining engineer Fredrik Idestam.

events.title: The 13th Amendment abolishes US slavery
events.note: It took effect once three-quarters of the states ratified it.

events.title: Nokia sells its phone business to Microsoft
events.note: The deal closed after Nokia had led the mobile market for years.

fact: The can opener was invented nearly 50 years after the tin can.

events.title: Babylonian tablets record cooking recipes
events.note: Yale's collection holds some of the oldest known written recipes.

events.title: Peter Durand patents the tin can
events.note: The patent was granted by King George III.

events.title: Ezra Warner patents a can opener
events.note: Before this, cans were opened with hammers and chisels.

events.title: John Landis Mason patents the Mason jar
events.note: A screw-top glass jar for home canning.

events.title: Birds Eye frozen foods go on sale
events.note: First sold in Springfield, Massachusetts.

fact: The steam locomotive is older than the bicycle: Trevithick's engine ran in 1804, Drais's 'running machine' in 1817.

events.title: Hero of Alexandria describes a steam-powered sphere
events.note: His aeolipile spun but did no useful work.

events.title: Trevithick's steam locomotive runs on rails
events.note: It hauled iron at Pen-y-darren in Wales.

events.title: Mount Tambora erupts
events.note: The largest volcanic eruption in recorded history.

events.title: Karl Drais rides his two-wheeled 'running machine'
events.note: A pedal-less ancestor of the bicycle.

events.title: Frankenstein is published
events.note: Mary Shelley began it during the cold, wet summer of 1816.

fact: William Herschel discovered Uranus in 1781 and wanted to name it after George III — the year Britain surrendered at Yorktown.

events.title: Aristarchus proposes a Sun-centred cosmos
events.note: The Greek astronomer put the Sun, not Earth, at the centre.

events.title: William Herschel discovers Uranus
events.note: The first planet discovered with a telescope.

events.title: The British surrender at Yorktown
events.note: The decisive defeat of the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: Neptune is discovered
events.note: Found close to where mathematics predicted it would be.

events.title: Neptune completes its first orbit since discovery
events.note: One Neptune year lasts about 165 Earth years.

fact: X-rays and cinema were both unveiled in late 1895, just seven weeks apart.

events.title: Ibn al-Haytham writes his Book of Optics
events.note: He explained vision as light entering the eye.

events.title: Daguerre's photography process is made public
events.note: The French government presented it as a gift to the world.

events.title: Wilhelm Röntgen discovers X-rays
events.note: One of his first X-ray images showed his wife's hand.

events.title: The Lumière brothers hold a paid film screening
events.note: Shown in the basement of the Grand Café in Paris.

events.title: Henri Becquerel discovers radioactivity
events.note: Uranium salts fogged photographic plates in the dark.

fact: Smallpox was declared eradicated just two weeks before Pac-Man reached Japanese arcades.

events.title: Pharaoh Ramesses V dies, apparently of smallpox
events.note: His mummy shows pustule-like marks.

events.title: Edward Jenner tests his smallpox vaccine
events.note: He inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with cowpox.

events.title: The WHO declares smallpox eradicated
events.note: The first human disease ever wiped out.

events.title: Mount St. Helens erupts
events.note: The blast removed the top of the mountain in Washington state.

events.title: Pac-Man is released in Japan
events.note: Its original Japanese name was Puck Man.

fact: Russia's Bolshoi Theatre is older than the United States — by about three months.

events.title: Battles of Lexington and Concord
events.note: The first battles of the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations
events.note: A founding text of modern economics.

events.title: Moscow's Bolshoi Theatre company is founded
events.note: Catherine the Great granted Prince Urusov a licence to stage shows.

events.title: The Declaration of Independence is adopted
events.note: Adopted by the Continental Congress in Philadelphia.

events.title: Captain Cook sets sail on his final voyage
events.note: He was killed in Hawaii during the expedition.

fact: The last passenger pigeon died just 17 days after the Panama Canal opened.

events.title: Archduke Franz Ferdinand is assassinated
events.note: Shot in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip.

events.title: Shackleton's Endurance sails from Plymouth
events.note: The ship was later crushed by Antarctic pack ice.

events.title: The Panama Canal opens
events.note: The SS Ancon made the first official transit.

events.title: Martha, the last passenger pigeon, dies
events.note: She died at Cincinnati Zoo.

events.title: The Christmas truce on the Western Front
events.note: Soldiers on both sides met in no man's land.

fact: England had three kings in 1066 — and Halley's Comet blazed overhead months before the Norman invasion.

events.title: Westminster Abbey is consecrated
events.note: King Edward the Confessor was too ill to attend.

events.title: Halley's Comet blazes over England
events.note: It was later stitched into the Bayeux Tapestry.

events.title: The Battle of Stamford Bridge
events.note: Harold II defeated the Norwegian king Harald Hardrada.

events.title: The Battle of Hastings
events.note: Harold II was killed by the invading Normans.

events.title: William the Conqueror is crowned
events.note: Crowned in Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day.

fact: The first Tour de France and the first World Series were both held in 1903 — the year the Wrights first flew.

events.title: Ford Motor Company is incorporated
events.note: Henry Ford was 39 years old.

events.title: The first Tour de France starts
events.note: Maurice Garin won the six-stage race.

events.title: The first World Series game is played
events.note: Boston beat Pittsburgh in the best-of-nine series.

events.title: Panama declares independence from Colombia
events.note: The US quickly backed it to secure a canal route.

events.title: Wright brothers make the first powered flight
events.note: The first flight at Kitty Hawk lasted 12 seconds.

fact: Ethiopia crushed Italy's army at Adwa just five weeks before the first modern Olympics opened.

events.title: King Ezana of Aksum adopts Christianity
events.note: Aksum was one of the first states to adopt Christianity.

events.title: Mansa Musa makes his pilgrimage to Mecca
events.note: The Mali emperor's lavish gold spending was remembered in Cairo for years.

events.title: The Berlin Conference on Africa opens
events.note: European powers set rules for claiming African territory.

events.title: Ethiopia defeats Italy at Adwa
events.note: It secured Ethiopian independence.

events.title: The first modern Olympics open in Athens
events.note: Athletes from 14 nations took part.

fact: Pakistan and India mark independence a day apart — on 14 and 15 August 1947.

events.title: Chandragupta founds the Maurya Empire
events.note: It grew to cover most of the Indian subcontinent.

events.title: Babur wins at Panipat, founding the Mughal Empire
events.note: His cannons helped defeat the Delhi Sultanate.

events.title: The English East India Company is chartered
events.note: Elizabeth I granted it a monopoly on trade to the East.

events.title: Pakistan becomes independent
events.note: Created by the partition of British India.

events.title: India becomes independent
events.note: Nehru gave his 'Tryst with Destiny' speech at midnight.

fact: Hiram Bingham reached Machu Picchu less than a month before the Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre.

events.title: The Pyramid of the Sun rises at Teotihuacan
events.note: One of the largest pyramids in the Americas.

events.title: The Inca build Machu Picchu
events.note: Probably an estate for the emperor Pachacuti.

events.title: Peru declares independence from Spain
events.note: Proclaimed in Lima by José de San Martín.

events.title: Hiram Bingham reaches Machu Picchu
events.note: A local farmer guided him to the ruins.

events.title: The Mona Lisa is stolen from the Louvre
events.note: Vincenzo Peruggia kept it for over two years.

fact: The Suez Canal and America's first transcontinental railroad both opened in 1869, six months apart.

events.title: Pharaoh Necho II starts a Nile–Red Sea canal
events.note: An early forerunner of the Suez Canal.

events.title: Golden spike completes a coast-to-coast US railroad
events.note: Driven at Promontory Summit, Utah.

events.title: The Suez Canal opens
events.note: It linked the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.

events.title: Egypt nationalises the Suez Canal
events.note: The move triggered the Suez Crisis.

events.title: The Aswan High Dam is completed
events.note: It created Lake Nasser on the Nile.

fact: The First Fleet founded Sydney in January 1788 — about 18 months before the storming of the Bastille.

events.title: Mungo Man is buried at Lake Mungo
events.note: Among the oldest known human burials in Australia.

events.title: Captain Cook lands at Botany Bay
events.note: He later claimed eastern Australia for Britain.

events.title: The First Fleet arrives at Sydney Cove
events.note: Eleven ships carried convicts, marines and officials.

events.title: Storming of the Bastille
events.note: A flashpoint of the French Revolution.

events.title: Sydney Opera House opens
events.note: Opened by Queen Elizabeth II.
